subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Ayrton Senna's Genius
description: A short lesson to help you apply Ayrton Senna's Genius.

hook.text: Ayrton Senna could feel rain on the track through his steering wheel before anyone else.

buildup.text: The Brazilian won three world titles by pushing himself and his car past limits others feared.

discovery.text: His 1988 qualifying lap at Monaco—1.4 seconds faster than the next car—is still considered superhuman.

twist.text: His intense rivalry with Alain Prost defined a decade and split the entire sport into two camps.

climax.text: Senna died at Imola in 1994, and his death transformed F1 safety standards forever.

punchline.text: The fastest driver ever made the sport safer by losing his life.

quiz.question: How many Formula One world titles did Ayrton Senna win?

details.summary: Ayrton Senna was a three-time Formula One world champion whose otherworldly car control, fierce competitiveness, and tragic death at Imola in 1994 made him the most revered racing driver in history.
details.whyItMatters: Senna's legacy transcends motorsport. His dedication, humanitarian work in Brazil, and untimely death transformed him into a cultural icon and drove major safety improvements in Formula One.
takeaways: He won three F1 world championships with McLaren
His wet-weather driving was considered supernaturally gifted
His death at Imola in 1994 triggered sweeping safety reforms in F1

faq.question: What made Senna faster than other drivers?
faq.answer: Senna combined extraordinary car feel with complete mental focus. He could extract performance in conditions that paralyzed rivals, most famously in his 1988 Monaco qualifying lap that was 1.4 seconds faster than second place.

faq.question: How did Senna's death change Formula One?
faq.answer: The FIA overhauled track safety with gravel traps, energy-absorbing barriers, stronger monocoques, and the HANS device. No driver died in an F1 race weekend for over 20 years after Senna's crash.
